title: Self Coding Agents — Colin Flaherty, Augment Code
talk_summary: Augment Code built a coding agent that wrote over 90% of a 20k-line codebase under human supervision. The transferable lessons are agent onboarding via a searchable knowledge base, bounded test-feedback loops, process-management tools, durable memory, and multi-source context.

takeaways.what_they_do: They keep markdown docs for tools, test commands, style guides, and unfamiliar systems, then let the agent dynamically retrieve them when it does not know something.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we add this into the context for the agent so it can dynamically go searching this

takeaways.what_they_do: The agent proposes a fix, runs tests, reads feedback, and repeats up to four times before finalizing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: run tests look at the feedback suggest another fix run test and do that four times
takeaways.numbers: 20% gain on internal bug-fix benchmark with 4 test-fix iterations; 4% gain from a 6-month newer foundation model

takeaways.technique: Tests as guardrails for hard edge cases
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat missing tests as the reason agents miss concurrency/cache defects, and use tests to increase trust and autonomy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we didn't have a test and because we didn't have a test the agent messed up

takeaways.technique: Subprocess tool with timeout and output capture
takeaways.what_they_do: They give the agent process-management tools to run subprocesses, read output, and avoid hanging on infinite loops.
takeaways.evidence_quote: not hanging if there's an infinite Loop in some test it wrote

takeaways.what_they_do: When the agent misses a useful fact, it writes a memory entry so future runs can reuse it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it called this memory tool to create a memory of the where where the Google credentials are stored

takeaways.what_they_do: They combine codebase, Slack, and third-party integration context rather than relying on one source.
takeaways.evidence_quote: good context is critical in all three of these tasks we needed to pull in some different context from some different sources
